# Anatomy of a STEP file {#sec-anatomy}

A STEP file is a plain text file whose structure is defined by ISO 10303-21 [@iso10303-21].
This chapter dissects a minimal but valid file so that every line is familiar before we look at the standard behind it.

## A complete example

@lst-minimal shows a file that defines nothing more than a coordinate system placed at the origin.
It is complete and can be saved as `placement.stp`.

```{#lst-minimal .default lst-cap="A minimal Part 21 file"}
ISO-10303-21;
HEADER;
FILE_DESCRIPTION(('A single axis placement'),'2;1');
FILE_NAME('placement.stp','2026-09-17T12:00:00',('Julian Chultarsky'),(''),'','','');
FILE_SCHEMA(('AP242_MANAGED_MODEL_BASED_3D_ENGINEERING_MIM_LF { 1 0 10303 442 3 1 4 }'));
ENDSEC;
DATA;
#1=CARTESIAN_POINT('origin',(0.,0.,0.));
#2=DIRECTION('z axis',(0.,0.,1.));
#3=DIRECTION('x axis',(1.,0.,0.));
#4=AXIS2_PLACEMENT_3D('',#1,#2,#3);
ENDSEC;
END-ISO-10303-21;
```

## The exchange structure

Every file has the same skeleton:

1. The opening keyword `ISO-10303-21;`.
2. A `HEADER` section that describes the file itself.
3. One or more `DATA` sections that hold the model.
4. The closing keyword `END-ISO-10303-21;`.

Keywords are case sensitive and always upper case.
Every statement ends with a semicolon, and whitespace outside of strings is insignificant, which is why some systems write an entire file on very long lines.

## The header section

The header always contains three entities, in this order.

`FILE_DESCRIPTION`
:   A free-text description of the contents and the *implementation level*.
    The value `'2;1'` is by far the most common and means conformance class 2 of Part 21 edition 1.

`FILE_NAME`
:   The file name, a timestamp in ISO 8601 form, the author, the organisation, the preprocessor that wrote the file, the originating system, and an authorisation string.
    Most of these are informational and frequently left empty.

`FILE_SCHEMA`
:   The name of the EXPRESS schema the data section conforms to.
    This is the single most important line for a reader, because it identifies the application protocol.
    The braces hold the ASN.1 object identifier of that schema.

## The data section

Each line in the data section is an *entity instance*.
Its parts are:

- an instance name, `#4`, which is unique within the file and used by other instances to refer to it;
- an entity type, `AXIS2_PLACEMENT_3D`, taken from the schema named in the header;
- a parenthesised list of attribute values in the order the schema declares them.

Attribute values can be strings, numbers, enumerations such as `.T.`, references to other instances such as `#1`, aggregates in parentheses, or the special tokens `$` (absent) and `*` (derived).
Instance numbers carry no meaning beyond identity: they need not be sequential and can appear in any order.

Reading the example bottom up, `#4` is a placement built from a point and two directions.
The two directions define the local Z and X axes; the Y axis is derived from them.
This pattern of small entities referring to each other by number is how a STEP file assembles everything from a single point to a full assembly.
